newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank reform session rescheduled for June 17.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank reform session rescheduled for June 17.

text.p: The U.S. House Banking Committee will hold a session to consider bank reform legislation on June 17, about one week later than previously announced, committee chairman Jim Leach said in a statement on Thursday.
The delay was "at the request of Democratic members," the Iowa Republican said.

Democrats on the banking panel had asked for a delay when they met with Leach on Wednesday. They were concerned that none of the reform proposals under consideration imposed sufficient legal safeguards on banks to protect consumers.
A new bill incorporating elements of earlier plans will be completed early next week, instead of on Friday as had been expected, Leach added.
